functions.name: asctime
functions.summary: Converts a broken-down time into a string like "Sun Sep 16 01:03:52 1973" followed by a new-line. Obsolescent: use strftime in new code.

params.name: timeptr
params.description: Pointer to the broken-down time to convert. Values outside their normal ranges, or a year below 1000 or above 9999, give undefined behavior.

functions.name: clock
functions.summary: Returns the processor time the program has used.

returns.description: The best approximation of the processor time used since an era tied to the program's start; divide by CLOCKS_PER_SEC to get seconds. Returns (clock_t)(-1) if the processor time isn't available, and an unspecified value if it can't be represented.

functions.name: ctime
functions.summary: Converts a calendar time to local time as a string, the same as asctime(localtime(timer)). Obsolescent: use strftime in new code.

params.name: timer
params.description: Pointer to the calendar time to convert.

returns.description: The pointer asctime returns for the converted local time.

functions.name: difftime
functions.summary: Computes the difference between two calendar times.

params.name: time1
params.description: The later calendar time.

params.name: time0
params.description: The earlier calendar time, subtracted from the first.

returns.description: The difference in seconds, as a double.

functions.name: mktime
functions.summary: Converts a broken-down local time into a calendar time, ignoring tm_wday and tm_yday and accepting out-of-range members. On success it rewrites the structure with normalized values.

params.name: timeptr
params.description: Pointer to the broken-down local time to convert. A negative tm_isdst asks the function to work out whether Daylight Saving Time applies.

returns.description: The calendar time as a time_t, or (time_t)(-1) if it can't be represented, in which case tm_wday is left unchanged.

functions.name: strftime
functions.summary: Formats a broken-down time into a string under the control of a format string, using the LC_TIME category of the current locale.
functions.signature: size_t strftime(char * restrict s, size_t maxsize, const char * restrict format, const struct tm * restrict timeptr);

params.name: s
params.description: Pointer to the array that receives the string.

params.name: maxsize
params.description: Maximum number of characters to write, terminating null character included.

params.name: format
params.description: Format string of ordinary characters and conversion specifiers such as %Y and %H.

params.name: timeptr
params.description: Pointer to the broken-down time to format.

returns.description: The number of characters written, not counting the terminating null character, if the result fits; otherwise zero, and the array contents are indeterminate.

functions.name: time

params.name: timer
params.description: Pointer to an object that also receives the result, or a null pointer.

returns.description: The best approximation of the current calendar time, or (time_t)(-1) if the calendar time isn't available.

functions.name: timegm
functions.summary: Converts a broken-down UTC time into a calendar time, ignoring tm_wday and tm_yday and accepting out-of-range members. On success it normalizes the structure and sets tm_wday and tm_yday.

params.name: timeptr
params.description: Pointer to the broken-down UTC time to convert.

returns.description: The calendar time as a time_t, or (time_t)(-1) if it can't be represented, in which case tm_wday is left unchanged.

functions.name: timespec_get
functions.summary: Stores the current calendar time, to nanosecond precision, in a timespec for the given time base.

params.name: ts
params.description: Pointer to the timespec that receives the time.

params.name: base
params.description: The time base, such as TIME_UTC.

returns.description: The nonzero value of the time base on success, or zero on failure.

functions.name: timespec_getres
functions.summary: Stores the resolution of timespec_get for a time base in a timespec.

params.name: ts
params.description: Pointer to the timespec that receives the resolution, or a null pointer.

params.name: base
params.description: The time base, such as TIME_UTC.

returns.description: The nonzero value of the time base if timespec_get supports it, otherwise zero.
